title: Regular Expression Matching
corePattern: Dynamic Programming over String Indices with Star Branching
interviewTips: Ask if pattern is always valid: every star has a preceding element, only '.' and '*' are special.
Trade-off: brute force recursion is simple but exponential, memoization gives O(m*n) with recursion overhead, bottom-up DP gives O(m*n) iteratively and is most robust for interviews.
Edge-case tip: empty string vs patterns like 'a*', 'a*b*', '.*' and trailing stars require careful base case handling.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Recursion
approaches.intuition: Match s[i:] against p[j:] recursively. If next pattern char is star, try zero occurrence by skipping it, or one-or-more by consuming one char of s if first chars match. Otherwise require first char match and advance both.
approaches.theory: Define dfs(i,j) as whether suffixes s[i:] and p[j:] match. Let first = i<m and (p[j]==s[i] or p[j]=='.'). If p[j+1]=='*', then dfs(i,j)=dfs(i,j+2) or (first and dfs(i+1,j)). Else dfs(i,j)=first and dfs(i+1,j+1). Base case j==n returns i==m. This explores all star choices.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each star creates two branches (skip vs consume), leading to exponential number of states in worst case like s=aaaa, p=a*a*a*a*. m=|s|, n=|p|.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion depth at most m+n due to advancing i or j along call stack, no memo table.

steps: dfs(0,0): first=true and p[1]==*, try dfs(0,2)
dfs(0,2): j==n but i!=m, returns false
dfs(1,0): first=true, try dfs(1,2)=false, then dfs(2,0)
dfs(2,0): try dfs(2,2)=true via zero occurrence, returns true

edgeCases: Empty s and empty p returns true
s='a', p='ab*' returns true via zero b
s='ab', p='.*' returns true via dot-star consuming all
Stack overflow on long inputs due to exponential calls

approaches.name: Approach 2: Top-Down DP with Memoization
approaches.intuition: Same recursion as brute force but many (i,j) states repeat. Cache result of dfs(i,j) so each pair is computed once.
approaches.theory: Number of distinct states is (m+1)*(n+1). Each state does O(1) work: check first match and at most two recursive calls. Memoization converts exponential recursion DAG into polynomial DP. Correctness follows from optimal substructure of suffix matching.

timeComplexity.explanation: At most (m+1)*(n+1) states, each computed once with O(1) work. m=|s|, n=|p|.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Memo table of size (m+1)*(n+1) plus recursion stack O(m+n).

steps: dfs(0,0): first=true, star case needs dfs(0,2) or dfs(1,0)
dfs(1,0): first=true, needs dfs(1,2) or dfs(2,0)
dfs(1,2)=false, dfs(2,0) needs dfs(2,2)=true => true propagates back

edgeCases: s empty, p='a*b*c*' => true via all zero occurrences
s='a', p='.*..' => false, dot-star cannot fix length mismatch
p ending with star, s longer than fixed prefix
Overlapping subproblems like '.*.*' benefit most from memo

approaches.name: Approach 3: Bottom-Up DP Table
approaches.intuition: Fill dp[i][j] = whether s[i:] matches p[j:] backwards from end to start, so dependencies dp[i][j+2], dp[i+1][j], dp[i+1][j+1] are already known.
approaches.theory: Same recurrence as recursion but evaluated iteratively in reverse order. Base dp[m][n]=true, dp[m][j] handles patterns that can match empty via stars. Iteration i from m down to 0, j from n-1 down to 0 guarantees needed future states are computed. Avoids recursion overhead and is optimal for production.

timeComplexity.explanation: Double loop over (m+1)*(n+1) table with O(1) transition per cell.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Full 2D boolean table. Can be optimized to O(n) by keeping only rows i and i+1 since transition uses current row j+2 and next row, but 2D is clearer and expected.

steps: row i=3: patterns with stars can match empty, e.g. dp[3][1] for a* is true
i=1,a vs a*: dp[1][1]=dp[1][3] or dp[2][1]=true
i=0,a vs c*a*: zero c then a* matches => dp[0][0]=true

edgeCases: s='mississippi', p='mis*is*p*.' => false, classic LeetCode case
p='.*' matches any s including empty
p with consecutive stars is invalid per constraints but code safely handles j+1 check
